subject: Post-call recap: performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider

Samir - thanks for the call today. Quick recap of the performance / SLO items we discussed and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan. Please flag anything I missed.

Key notes from the call:
- Current provider (managed on-prem setup): end-to-end p95 ~ 320 ms, p99 ~ 780 ms for your main scoring endpoint (350 tokens average).
- FinLytics target: p95 <= 200 ms and p99 <= 400 ms end-to-end for production traffic; hard requirement for streaming first-byte p95 <= 100 ms for interactive tracers.
- Traffic profile: sustained 120 req/s (avg), typical concurrency target 40-60, and ability to handle bursts up to 250 req/s for short windows. Avg request size ~350 tokens, peak up to 1k tokens.
- Streaming: required for your product (token-by-token UI), buffer/first-byte latency is critical.

How Redwood hosted API maps to this:
- Streaming support with chunked responses (we can measure 1st-byte p95 in staging).
- Continuous batching and prefix/KV caching reduce per-token latency for repeat prefixes (relevant to your prompt patterns).
- We can run a 48-72 hour production-profile perf test from your region (us-east) against a hosted test endpoint to validate p95/p99 and throughput under realistic concurrency.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) You share 24-48 hours of representative traces (sample) and a small synthetic traffic spec (I attached a template).
2) Laura to propose a perf-test plan (load shape, benchmarks, acceptance criteria).
3) We run a hosted perf test and share p95/p99 histograms + actionable items (caching, batching, autoscale).
4) Decide whether Dedicated capacity needed for committed SLAs (if hosted misses targets under multi-tenant noise).

Attachments: redwood_perf_p95p99_summary.pdf (summary + measurement plan), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MAM template).

Thanks - I'll loop in Laura on the technical plan.

-
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider

Marissa - thanks for the concise recap. That matches our internal notes. Couple of clarifications and answers:
- The numbers I quoted are end-to-end (client -> our edge -> model -> client). Our current provider is a hybrid managed service with some regional proxies which add variability during peaks.
- Streaming first byte is a hard requirement - we can tolerate up to 120 ms p95 for first-byte only if end-to-end still meets p95<=200 ms. Otherwise first-byte p95 <= 100 ms.
- Concurrency: our UI needs sustained concurrency of 50 for interactive sessions. Batch jobs (non-streaming) run in evenings and can be deprioritized.

We'll attach a small sample of latency traces and a header describing traffic shape. Attaching now.

-
Samir Khan
Head of Engineering | FinLytics
samir.khan@finlytics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider

Samir - appreciate the traces. Quick technical notes / ask so we can scope the perf run: 

Questions for the traces you attached:
- Can you confirm whether these traces include client-side RTT (network) or are they server-logged end-to-end? We want to separate user-network variance vs model-inference time.
- Please indicate the tokenization for the sample (we need tokens/request distribution).

Proposed perf test plan (high level):
- Environment: Redwood hosted (us-east) single-region test endpoint configured with same model + quantization profile you run in prod.
- Load shape: 48 hours with a ramp to 120 req/s sustained, 1-min bursts to 250 req/s every 4 hours to simulate spikes.
- Concurrency: run at concurrency = 50 steady and also evaluate concurrency=80 for headroom.
- Metrics collected: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency (stream start), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and per-request kernel breakdown.
- Acceptance: p95 <= 200 ms and p99 <= 400 ms end-to-end; first-byte p95 <= 100 ms (or <=120 ms if p95 still <=200 ms).

If the hosted run misses targets due to multi-tenant variance, we'll propose either Dedicated pool sizing or simple routing + regional pinning to meet SLOs.

I will prepare the exact load script and share it (JMeter/Locust spec) - please confirm the traces file contains server timestamps.

-
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider

Laura - good plan. A couple quick answers:
- Traces: attached "finlytics_latency_traces_sample.json" - these are server-side end-to-end timestamps (we included client timestamp too). Tokenization: we use standard BPE, avg tokens/request = 352.
- We can run the hosted perf test on a staging key if you provide it - want to make sure nothing in the tests hits prod routing or billing.

Attachments: finlytics_latency_traces_sample.json (sample traces).

-
Samir Khan
Head of Engineering | FinLytics
samir.khan@finlytics.com

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider

Perfect - thanks Samir. Next actions: 
- Laura will share the load script + staging endpoint details by EOD PST today.
- Samir / Priya to confirm traces include server timestamps (noted above) and drop any additional sample prompts that represent the 10% high-length tail.
- I'll create the MAM in the HubSpot deal and add milestones: Perf test, Analysis, Decision (Hosted vs Dedicated). You should see the HubSpot link in related links once I add it.

If hosted perf test hits targets, we'll proceed to procurement/PO discussion (Aditya will lead commercial terms). If not, we'll scope Dedicated sizing and prioritize a short pilot.

Looking forward - I'll follow up with calendar invites for a kickoff.

-
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
